## Operator-delegated rotation plan

This ticket completes the remaining externally anchored secret rotations from the value_wo state-remediation follow-up. The operator has already rotated and updated SSM for these names, so this task records/health-checks them but does not re-rotate them: `/rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key`, `/rebar/prod/jira-api-token`, `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`, `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`, `/rebar/prod/g2p-github-pat`, `/rebar/prod/reviewbot-tickets-pat`, `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-copilot`, `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-codex`, `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-claude`, and `/rebar/prod/mcp-tickets-pat`.

Operator carve-outs: `github-oauth-client-id`, `github-oauth-client-secret`, and `/auth-solutions/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are not rotatable by this operator because the needed third-party access is unavailable. `/rebar/prod/gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key` is deferred by operator decision because rotating it would break clients' pinned known_hosts entries.

## Scope for this task

Rotate exactly these five remaining rotatable secrets, one at a time, using the existing provisioning/runbook patterns and never recording secret values:

1. `/rebar/prod/github-replication-deploy-key`: generate a fresh passphrase-free ed25519 keypair; register the public key as a write-enabled deploy key on `navapbc/rebar` using the `rebar-gerrit-replication` deploy-key convention (unique rotation title if the old title is still present); overwrite the SSM SecureString with the private key; after redeploy verifies Gerrit→GitHub replication is healthy, delete the retired GitHub deploy key.
2. `/rebar/prod/ci-gerrit-ssh-key`: generate a fresh passphrase-free ed25519 keypair; add the public key to the `rebar-ci-bot` Gerrit account (overlap with old key); overwrite the SSM SecureString with the private key and update the GitHub Actions `GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY` secret so CI vote-back uses it; after verification remove the retired public key from the account.
3. `/auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET`: generate a fresh 48-character value with the existing `openssl rand -base64 36 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 48` convention; overwrite the SSM SecureString; redeploy/recreate the auth host Lambda per `infra/runbooks/sso-auth-host.md`. This intentionally invalidates active SSO sessions.
4. `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key`: generate a fresh passphrase-free ed25519 keypair; overwrite the SSM SecureString with the private key; update GitHub Actions `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY`; add the new public key to the Rebar Bot identity `unsinkable-varying-pelican` (`594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`) using `rebar identity key add`, leaving the old key registered for historical signatures unless tooling refuses.
5. `/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key`: generate a fresh passphrase-free ed25519 keypair; overwrite the SSM SecureString with the private key; update the trusted environment registration for env `9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65` using `rebar trusted-env add` in a separate worktree/change (do not edit the main checkout), leaving the old public key present for historical cert verification unless tooling requires a retire step. Enforcement is currently advisory/deferred.

## Safety / sequencing

- Do not use any `--force` or equivalent rebar force parameter.
- Never echo, log, commit, or comment secret values. Report only secret names, SSM version numbers, key ids/titles, and health evidence.
- Use `aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite --type SecureString` for writes, and verify each write only with `aws ssm get-parameter --name <name> --query Parameter.Version` without `--with-decryption`.
- Use scratch/key material only outside the repository checkout (session artifact directory), chmod 0600, and remove it after provisioning.
- Before any redeploy/restart that could affect Gerrit, inspect `deserved-rubidium-pussycat` and coordinate with the owner of the Gerrit missing-tree investigation. Do not restart Gerrit or touch Gerrit git data.
- Prefer zero-downtime consumers: re-materialize SSM secrets on-box with `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`, use the validated secrets-only autodeploy/blue-green pattern for review-bot and MCP, and avoid Gerrit container restarts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For each of the five in-scope secrets, a new value/key is generated and written to its SSM SecureString; the post-write SSM `Parameter.Version` is recorded and is greater than the pre-rotation version.
- [ ] External trust stores are updated: GitHub deploy key added, Gerrit `rebar-ci-bot` public key added, Rebar Bot identity keyring extended, op-cert trusted environment keyring extended, and GitHub Actions secrets updated where applicable.
- [ ] Retired overlapping keys are removed only after successful verification: old GitHub replication deploy key deleted after replication proves healthy; old CI Gerrit SSH public key removed after CI vote-back proves healthy; old Rebar Bot/opcert public keys stay registered for historical verification unless tooling dictates otherwise.
- [ ] Consumers are redeployed/restarted with minimal downtime: review-bot/opcert/MCP pick up re-materialized SSM secrets, auth host is refreshed for the cookie secret, and Gerrit itself is not restarted or its git data touched during the open P1 investigation.
- [ ] Health verification records Gerrit reachability, review-bot health, Gerrit→GitHub mirror replication health, MCP `/health`, op-cert health, CI vote-back or equivalent verification, and SSO login-page/authorize load.
- [ ] Completion comments name the secret names, SSM version numbers, external registration/deletion evidence, redeploy timing, health checks, operator carve-outs, and deferred host-key decision, and contain no secret values.
